annotation_description: World Breaker is the only card in hand with mana value 7+ that can be imprinted on Ugin's Labyrinth. Without it, Ugin's Labyrinth only produces {C} instead of {C}{C}, severely weakening the hand's mana acceleration. The synergy between these two cards is the primary reason to keep this hand.

message: Select a card (1 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: Bottoming Shifting Woodland leaves no Forest in hand, making Utopia Sprawl uncastable and stranding it. Shifting Woodland + Utopia Sprawl + Eldrazi Temple would have enabled a turn 2 Sowing Mycospawn (the deck's key play). Ugin's Labyrinth is strictly worse than Eldrazi Temple here since there's no 7+ MV card to imprint, making it redundant colorless production.

Utopia Sprawl enchanting the opponent's Temple Garden gives the OPPONENT the extra mana (the card says 'its controller adds an additional one mana'). Qwen3 Libby spent a card and mana to accelerate their opponent.

Winternight Stories has Harmonize (can be cast from graveyard), making it the ideal discard since it retains most of its value in the graveyard. Discarding Lightning Bolt instead loses a premium interactive spell permanently.

Qwen3 Libby passed their main phase without casting Sire of Seven Deaths, a 7/7 with first strike, vigilance, menace, trample, reach, lifelink, and ward-pay 7 life. They had sufficient mana (7+ available from their lands and Talisman, including Eldrazi Temple for {C}{C}). The opponent at 17 life with only a tapped Doorkeeper Thrull and limited mana couldn't effectively answer this threat.

Winternight Stories has Harmonize, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard - which means discarding it doesn't fully lose the card. However, discarding a second copy of Scion of Draco (which costs 8+ mana with only 2 basic land types, and is a duplicate) would preserve the more flexible spell while losing a card that's extremely difficult to cast in the current board state.

Qwen3 Libby has Sire of Seven Deaths in hand and enough mana to cast it (7 colorless available from Ugin's Labyrinth x2, Eldrazi Temple, Talisman, Ghost Quarter, plus colored lands). The opponent is at 14 life with only a tapped Doorkeeper Thrull. Sire of Seven Deaths (7/7 first strike, vigilance, menace, trample, lifelink, ward-pay 7 life) would be nearly unanswerable and threatens lethal in 2 attacks while gaining massive life.

Qwen3 Libby declined to cast Kozilek's Return during combat, taking 1 unnecessary damage from Doorkeeper Thrull. Casting it now would kill the Thrull (2 damage to a 1/2), save 1 life, and importantly put Kozilek's Return into the graveyard to set up the 5-damage trigger when casting Sire of Seven Deaths next turn.

With opponent at 11 life and only a tapped Doorkeeper Thrull on board, Sire of Seven Deaths (7/7 menace, trample, first strike, lifelink, vigilance with ward-pay 7 life) would likely end the game in 1-2 attacks. Menace means the single Thrull can't block alone, and trample pushes damage through. Ward-pay 7 life at 11 hp makes it nearly impossible to remove. World Breaker is a solid play that cripples their mana, but Sire closes the game faster.

Qwen3 Libby declined to cast Sire of Seven Deaths (7/7 with first strike, vigilance, menace, trample, lifelink, ward-pay 7 life) when the opponent is at exactly 7 life with a tapped board. The Sire is essentially untargetable (ward kills them) and represents lethal next turn alongside Sowing Mycospawn (7+3=10 with menace+trample). The opponent cannot meaningfully interact with it.
